positive.prompt: Write the low-level design for task 3 before I start implementing it
Before coding this subtask, work out the function signatures, edge cases, and error handling
Decide the retry, idempotency, and concurrency behaviour for this task before we write the code

negative.prompt: Write a failing test that reproduces this bug, then fix it
Implement this feature in small slices, testing each one before moving on
Design the system architecture for this story and decide which services talk to each other

evals.prompt: Task 2 in the plan is next. Write its low-level design note before implementing it.
evals.expected_output: A short design note added to the task entry: edge contracts, invariants, flow with failure branches, failure policy, security line, observability line, and the test cases they imply
expectations: The note is added to the Task 2 entry in the plan file and stays short (roughly 5 to 15 lines of design, not a long spec)
The note states the task's function signature or types at its edges with one concrete example
Out-of-order events and invalid transitions are handled by citing the C3 and C4 contracts rather than re-deriving or contradicting them

The note deals explicitly with the same event reaching the worker twice (C6 at-least-once delivery), either with data that already exists or by escalating the shared-contract change it needs, instead of leaving duplicate history rows to chance
The security line is not a bare n/a: because the worker has no caller, it names the trust boundary it relies on (signature verification at the webhook) and any fields that must not be logged
Each edge case and failure rule in the note maps to at least one listed test case
Any change to a shared table or contract is escalated rather than silently designed into the task
